title: Enterprise exec briefing accelerator + client quarterly storyboard
content:
PURPOSE:
This file is a single-sheet storyboard + email toolkit to accelerate executive sponsor briefings and the customer-facing quarterly recap. Use this when prepping a 20–30 minute sponsor meeting (exec-to-exec) plus a follow-up recap email. Designed to be lightweight, repeatable, and measurable so CS and Sales can align asks to renewal outcomes.

HOW TO USE (2 minutes):
- Pick the 3-slide storyboard (Impact, Health, Ask).
- Populate the KPIs snapshot below with current numbers.
- Share the 1-page pre-read 48–72 hours ahead.
- Run the 20-min meeting with the agenda below, capture decisions, send the short recap email within 24 hours.

ONE-PAGER (top of pre-read) — "Executive Snapshot" (single page, 1:30 read)
- Header: Customer name | Redwood account lead | Meeting date | Renewal window
- Key outcomes since last QBR (3 bullets): e.g., "Reduced inference unit cost by 18% via quantization profile"; "Stable 99.92% uptime across prod routes"; "2 pilot apps onboarded to Dedicated capacity"
- KPI headline row (single line each): 
  - Usage trend: M/M calls (+12%) | Avg tokens/day (240M) | Peak RPS (85)
  - Performance: Median token latency (38ms) | 95th pct latency (120ms)
  - Economics: Cost per 1k tokens (USD 0.52) | Estimated monthly bill (USD 68k)
- Health summary (green/amber/red + 1 sentence): Technology, Adoption, Business Impact
- Top 3 risks and mitigations: concise, owner + ETA
- Renewal posture & asks: recommended concession ladder and target next steps

3-SLIDE STORYBOARD (meeting flow)
Slide 1 — The Value Story (5 minutes)
- 2-line customer problem framing (what they solved with Redwood)
- Before/after metrics (baseline → current) with percent delta
- One short customer quote or product example (real behavior)

Slide 2 — Health & Ops (8 minutes)
- Topline SLA & performance metrics (uptime, latency percentiles, error rates)
- Recent operational events (incidents, rollouts) + action taken
- Adoption signals (active routes, active teams, feature usage e.g., streaming)
- Cost optimization summary (batching/cache saved X% last quarter)

Slide 3 — Ask & Roadmap (5–7 minutes)
- Renewal ladder: Tiered ask with outcomes attached (see Ask Ladder)
- Near-term roadmap items that matter for exec (VPC/KMS, Dedicated capacity commit, custom SLAs)
- Decision request and suggested next steps (who signs, timeline)

MEETING AGENDA (20 minutes total)
- 00:00 — Quick intros & objective (2 min)
- 00:02 — Value story (5 min)
- 00:07 — Health & ops (8 min)
- 00:15 — Ask & alignment (5 min)
- 00:20 — Confirm owners & next steps (1–2 min)

ASK LADDER (examples - pick one set to use)
- Level 1 (low friction): 6–12 month usage commitment (no price change) → outcome: reserved throughput & price stability
- Level 2 (preferred): Annual Dedicated reservation (x GPUs) with 10% discount → outcome: predictable latency and unit economics
- Level 3 (strategic): Private deployment + enterprise SLA (custom contract) → outcome: data locality + extended support
Include clear success metrics per level (throughput, latency SLO, cost delta).

RISK HEATMAP (one line each)
- Tech: High if daily error spikes or major regressions (owner: SRE)
- Adoption: Amber if only 1 team driving >70% of routes (owner: CS lead)
- Commercial: Red if renewal decision >60 days out with stalled exec contact (owner: AE)

KPIs SNAPSHOT (copy into slide 1 or pre-read table)
- Billing metrics: current MRR / forecasted ARR / churn estimate
- Usage: MAU of routes, active tokens/day, % growth M/M
- Perf: median token latency, p95 token latency, error rate %
- Efficiency: tokens per $1000, cache hit %, avg batch size

CUSTOMER-FACING QUARTERLY RECAP EMAIL (SHORT — for execs)
Subject: Q3 recap & next steps for [Customer Name] — quick update from Redwood
Hi [Exec first name],
Thanks for the time today — quick recap from our end and proposed next steps.
What moved the needle:
- Inference cost down ~18% quarter-over-quarter (quantization + smarter batching)
- Median token latency improved to 38ms (p95 120ms)
- Two new product teams launched pilots on Dedicated capacity
Risks we’re watching:
- One team’s test route showing error spikes during peak — SRE remediation planned for next week
Ask:
- Recommend committing to a 12-month reserved capacity plan to lock in current unit economics and priority capacity scheduling.
Next steps:
- I’ll share the 1-page pre-read and proposed contract terms by EOD Thursday. Can we schedule a 20-min follow up next week to confirm?
Thanks,
[Riley Chen] — Customer Success

CUSTOMER-FACING QUARTERLY RECAP EMAIL (DETAILED — for broader exec + product audience)
Subject: [Customer Name] Q3 outcomes, ops summary & renewal options
Hi [Name],
Attached is a one-page executive snapshot and the 3-slide storyboard we reviewed. Highlights:
- Business impact: lower per-token costs, faster inference, and two revenue-facing pilots now in staging.
- Operational summary: 99.92% uptime, two minor incidents resolved with permanent rollouts.
- Roadmap & asks: Recommend Level 2 reservation to maintain throughput for new pilots; discuss Private deployment timeline if data-locality remains a priority.
Appendix includes the KPI table, incident timeline, and cost projection for each renewal option. Please reply with availability for a 20-min alignment call.
Best,
[Riley Chen]

PRE-READ CHECKLIST (for CS owner before sending)
- [ ] Fill KPI table and sanity-check numbers with billing (finance cc)
- [ ] Confirm incident summaries with SRE + attach postmortems (if any)
- [ ] Draft renewal terms with AE (concessions + timeline)
- [ ] Add a customer quote or product screenshot to the Value slide
- [ ] Send to execs 48–72 hours prior with calendar invite

FOLLOW-UP & ACTIONS (post-meeting)
- Capture decisions in the recap email (24 hours)
- Raise renewal ticket in SFDC/Hub with target close date (AE)
- Schedule technical deep-dive for implementation owners (if Level 2/3 chosen)
- Weekly sync with customer champion until renewal is closed

NOTES & TACTICS (quick tips learned)
- Execs respond to short economics + a single customer story — keep the pitch lean.
- Use a clear ask ladder; execs appreciate choice framed as outcomes, not price.
- If adoption is concentrated, propose concrete enablement (office hours, SDK templates) tied to a 30–60–90 plan.

ATTACHMENTS (suggested)
- 1-page executive snapshot (PDF)
- 3-slide storyboard deck (pptx)
- KPI export (sheet) and billing projection (sheet)
- Incident summaries (pdf)

ENDPOINT: This template should make exec outreach repeatable and low-friction. Keep one copy per customer in Drive; iterate after each QBR (replace metrics and the single case study).

=== SAMPLE FILL (example numbers to copy) ===
- Avg tokens/day: 240,000,000
- Monthly estimated bill: $68,000
- Median token latency: 38ms; p95: 120ms
- Cache hit rate: 42%
- Active routes: 18; pilot teams: 2

If you want, I can generate a matching 1-page PDF template and a 3-slide deck skeleton (pptx) that uses these sections — drop a note and I’ll create the files for review.
